scope: 30 generated historical interpretations and 2 unchanged real modern reference photographs across eight sets; 7 corrective edits preserved in generation history.
historical_status: Research-informed artistic interpretations, not authenticated reconstructions.

sources.title: Old Handicrafts industries in Assam
sources.note: Government of Assam craft survey. Supports weaving, pottery, smithing, bamboo work and carpentry as regional traditions; explicitly discusses eighteenth-century silk trade. Not a dated plan for a workshop or costume.

sources.title: Miscellaneous Arts & Crafts of Assam
sources.note: Regional cultural survey identifies carpenters making houses, ploughs, looms and boats. Contemporary observations are comparative evidence for materials and craft vocabulary, not proof of an unchanged eighteenth-century technique.

sources.title: Textiles of Assam
sources.note: Regional textile overview distinguishes plains posted looms from backstrap looms. Use a timber frame loom; neither the exact pattern nor the assembled workshop is authenticated.

sources.title: Jakhoi and Khaloi: Introduction
sources.note: Design documentation of bamboo craft in Barpeta and Nalbari. Comparative reference for basket weave and fishing gear. Does not date specific forms to the Ahom period.

sources.title: Traditional Craft and Gears in Assam and Different Fishing Methods
sources.note: Assam Agricultural University documentation of traditional small wooden boats and manual propulsion. Modern documentation only; exclude engines, plastic and modern boat covers.

sources.title: Lachit Barphukan and His Times, S. K. Bhuyan
sources.note: Historical study, printed p.150: describes seventeenth-century dockyards and distinguishes boat-building and boat-plying khels. Supports military preparation themes, not an exact vessel reconstruction or a uniform regulation.

sources.title: A History of Assam, Edward Gait
sources.note: Indexed historical text includes a translated seventeenth-century description of Assamese war boats and abundant water transport. Use only as corroboration of river traffic; do not turn reported boat counts into established measurements.

sources.title: Publication, Directorate of Historical and Antiquarian Studies
sources.note: Official catalogue identifies published Ahom, Assamese, Kachari and Jayantia chronicles and the Tungkhungia Buranji translation. Establishes the documentary tradition; does not reconstruct a particular writing room.

sources.title: Manuscript Painting of Assam: Historical and Contemporary Perspectives
sources.note: Scholarly overview identifies sanchi bark and cotton writing supports, preparation through curing/seasoning/polishing and traditional ink. Use oblong unbound bark folios. No invented legible historical passage.

sources.title: In Conversation with Chittaranjan Borah
sources.note: Practitioner interview on sanchi-bark manuscript practice. Contemporary technical comparison; does not establish the dress or room layout of an eighteenth-century scribe.

sources.title: Ahom Raja’s Palace, ASI
sources.note: ASI distinguishes the 1540 impermanent palace from the surviving masonry edifice dated 1752. The historical comparison uses circa 1760. Maintained finishes and lost surroundings are interpretive.

sources.title: Rang Ghar, Incredible India
sources.note: Ministry of Tourism identifies Pramatta Singha, the two-storey sports pavilion and its boat-like roof. Circa 1760 is later than his reign. Modern park paths must not enter the historical view.

sources.title: The Architecture of Ahoms, INTACH documentation panels
sources.note: Architectural documentation, indexed Rang Ghar panel, describes the secular pavilion and arches. Use to corroborate building identity and form, not to convert temple forms into houses.

sources.title: Joysagar Tank and Temples, Sivasagar district
sources.note: District account attributes the tank to Rudra Singha in memory of Joymoti but gives 1707; other official accounts give 1697. Use the reign, circa 1696–1714, rather than resolve the discrepancy by assertion. Labour arrangement, excavation tools and staging are interpretive.

sources.title: Sivasagar District Disaster Management Plan 2025–26
sources.note: Historical tourism section gives Joysagar as 1697 and Rang Ghar under Pramatta Singha. Other palace details conflict with ASI, so this document is not used to date the palace.

sources.title: Political Ecology of an Environmental Crisis in the Brahmaputra Valley, Assam
sources.note: Scholarly discussion of historical flood control traces Ahom embankment building and later expansion. Supports an earthwork maintenance theme, not the location, dimensions or performance of the depicted bund.

sources.title: A Study of Markets, Trade Routes, and Currency under the Ahom Government — Raja Doley (2025)
sources.note: Historical article discusses hats, goods and river/overland trading routes. Supports the market theme; does not supply stall plans, exact dress, a rice-for-cloth exchange rate or an exclusively barter economy.

sources.title: Commerce, Merchants and Markets in the Brahmaputra Valley c.1800–1900 — Nabanita Sharma (2019)
sources.note: Study of pre-colonial/colonial transition based on chronicles and archival sources. Used as a caution against flattening changing commerce into a timeless village-market stereotype. Its nineteenth-century evidence does not directly date a scene to 1750.
